solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Harmonised short anthem penned by revolutionary

indicators.note: penned by says the shortened anthem is enclosed, as if in a pen, by the revolutionary

parts.note: a red is a revolutionary, a communist

indicators.note: short says the word for anthem loses its final letter

parts.note: a hymn is an anthem of praise

explanation.surface: A choir sings a cut-down anthem written by a revolutionary.
explanation.definitionFit: Lines that rhyme share end sounds, so they are in a kind of harmony with each other.

clue.text: Very large portion of chicken or moussaka

indicators.note: portion of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A diner is served a huge helping of chicken or moussaka.
explanation.definitionFit: Something vast or huge is extremely big in size, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Care about first person to enter retirement

indicators.note: to enter says the pieces before it go inside the word for retirement

parts.note: retirement in the sense of withdrawal from company, being alone
C, short for circa, means about
the first person singular pronoun is I

explanation.surface: Someone retiring is looked after; the first to go into retirement gets attention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to enter' puts C and I inside SOLITUDE.
explanation.definitionFit: Solicitude is anxious concern or attentiveness for someone, which is a kind of care.

clue.text: Represent someone myself — that's provided for everything

indicators.note: for says the word for provided stands in place of the word for everything

parts.note: speaking for myself as a person, i.e. personally
all means everything
if means provided, as in 'provided that'

explanation.surface: A speaker insists on representing someone in person, as long as it covers everything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' swaps ALL out of PERSONALLY and puts IF in its place.
explanation.definitionFit: To embody or typify a quality is to stand for it, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Impressive online image?

parts.note: E is the prefix for electronic or online, as in e-mail
pic is short for picture, an image

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a striking picture seen on the internet is impressive.
explanation.definitionFit: In modern slang something epic is grand or awesome, hence very striking.

clue.text: Perhaps select pictures for office in religious establishment

definitions.meaning: to choose and arrange works for an exhibition, as a gallery does
an assistant parish priest's post in the Church

explanation.surface: A cleric chooses artwork for an office in a church building.
explanation.definitionFit: A gallery organiser chooses exhibits; a junior cleric assisting a vicar holds the church post of the same name.

clue.text: Social workers' brief ultimately failed to protect child

indicators.note: to protect says the trimmed word wraps round the child, shielding it
ultimately failed says the final letter of the word for brief is lost

parts.note: terse means brief, short in speech
a mite is a small child

explanation.surface: Social workers' short report failed to keep a child safe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Social workers' are not care staff but insects living in colonies.
explanation.definitionFit: These insects live in highly organised colonies with worker castes, so they are social workers.

clue.text: Charity worker on strike

parts.note: a hand is a manual worker, as in farmhand
workers who strike are out

explanation.surface: An employee of a charity has walked out on strike.
explanation.definitionFit: Charity can mean alms, money or goods given free to the needy, which is a dole or gift.

clue.text: Post on social media that's short and sweet

indicators.note: short says the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a tweet is a post on the platform once called Twitter

explanation.surface: An online message is brief and pleasant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' clips the last T from TWEET.
explanation.definitionFit: Twee is a British word for affectedly cute or quaint, so sweet in a cloying way.

clue.text: After losing case, tyrant has to employ advocate

indicators.note: losing case says the outer letters, the casing of the word for tyrant, are removed

parts.note: a despot is a tyrant
to use something is to employ it

explanation.surface: A dictator, having lost a court case, hires a lawyer.
explanation.definitionFit: To espouse a cause is to support or champion it, as an advocate does.

clue.text: Callous crime ransacked bar

indicators.note: ransacked means turned upside down, so these letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: bar can mean except, as does less: 'all bar one' or 'all less one'

explanation.surface: A heartless crime saw a pub ransacked.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone without pity is hard-hearted and unfeeling, so the words are synonyms.

clue.text: Flock initially caused damage

indicators.note: initially says only the opening letter of the next word is used

parts.note: harm means damage

explanation.surface: A flock of birds first caused damage.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of goldfinches is traditionally called a charm, a collective noun like flock.

clue.text: Police officer impounds stolen material covering sensitive areas

indicators.note: impounds says the officer's letters enclose the next piece, as if seized

parts.note: DI is a Detective Inspector
hot is slang for stolen

explanation.surface: A detective seizes stolen cloth covering private parts.
explanation.definitionFit: A dhoti is the loincloth worn by men in India, a wrapped garment covering the groin.

clue.text: Beginning to develop new way to go up in the world

parts.words: way to go up in the world
parts.note: an ascent is a climb, a way of rising

explanation.surface: A new route to social advancement is starting to emerge.
explanation.definitionFit: Something emerging or embryonic is just coming into existence and starting to grow.

clue.text: Exotic island bordering Guam distributed potpourri

indicators.note: bordering says the first jumble lies on either side of the second
exotic means strange or foreign, so these letters take on an unfamiliar arrangement
distributed means spread around, so these letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: A foreign island near Guam handed out fragrant dried petals.
explanation.walkthrough: Two separate anagrams: one jumbled word is wrapped around the other.
explanation.definitionFit: A salmagundi is a mixed salad and, by extension, a medley or miscellany of assorted items.

clue.text: Villain misled counsel about daughter whose body's disappeared

indicators.note: about says the jumbled letters go round the remaining pair
misled means led astray, so these letters are sent the wrong way into a new order
with its body gone only the first and last letters of the word remain

explanation.surface: A villain deceived a lawyer about a daughter whose body was never found.
explanation.walkthrough: 'whose body's disappeared' leaves only the first and last letters of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A rogue or rascal is a dishonest, unprincipled person, a synonym for a wrongdoer.

clue.text: Curse felon's ruse to change desirable property

indicators.note: to change says these letters must alter their order

explanation.surface: A criminal's trick changes hands over a desirable house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to change' rearranges all the letters of CURSE FELONS RUSE. 'property' looks like real estate but means a quality.
explanation.definitionFit: Ingenuity in finding ways round problems is a valued quality or attribute, a property in that sense.

clue.text: Swede's routine win accepted by driving club

parts.note: a rut is a dull routine

indicators.note: accepted by says the word for win goes inside the club's letters

parts.note: the AA is the Automobile Association, a British motoring organisation
to bag something is to win it

explanation.surface: A Swedish golfer's usual win is welcomed by the club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swede' is the vegetable, not a person from Sweden; the 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Rutabaga is the North American name for the root vegetable the British call swede.

clue.text: Trade fair has allowed for nothing specific

indicators.note: for says the word for allowed is put in place of the letter for nothing

parts.note: an expo is an exhibition or trade fair
O looks like zero, nothing
licit means allowed, lawful

explanation.surface: A trade fair has made allowance for nothing specific.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' swaps the final O of EXPO for LICIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Something stated clearly and in detail leaves nothing implied, so it is precise and definite.

clue.text: Letter from abroad captures skilful pictorial representation

indicators.note: captures says the Greek letter encloses the next piece

parts.note: tau is a letter of the Greek alphabet
able means skilful

explanation.surface: A letter from overseas includes a clever picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A tableau is a picturesque scene or a group of people posed to depict one.

clue.text: Large plant beginning to bottle four different types of claret

indicators.note: beginning to says only the opening letter of the next word is used

parts.note: claret is British slang for blood; four blood groups are A, O, B and AB

explanation.surface: A wine buff starts bottling four kinds of Bordeaux red.
explanation.walkthrough: 'claret' looks like wine but is slang for blood.
explanation.definitionFit: The baobab is a huge African tree with a massively thick trunk, hence a large plant.

clue.text: Setter related to Serpent?

definitions.meaning: a savoury jelly that sets meat or fish in a mould
an archaic word for the asp, a venomous snake; the question mark flags the old usage

explanation.surface: The puzzle's compiler, Serpent, wonders whether a setter is a relative.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter of this puzzle calls himself Serpent, so 'Setter' looks like the compiler; it is a jelly that sets.
explanation.definitionFit: Savoury jelly sets food in a mould; in old usage the same word named a small venomous snake.

clue.text: Transport company resent moving base south

indicators.note: moving says one letter is shifted to a new place within the word
in a down clue south is further down, so the letter goes lower in the word

parts.note: to envy is to resent
e is the base of natural logarithms

explanation.surface: A haulage firm resents relocating its base to the south.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving base south' moves the E of ENVY two places down, giving NVEY.
explanation.definitionFit: To convey goods is to carry them from one place to another.

clue.text: African expedition exposed overseas, perhaps

indicators.note: exposed means stripped of its outer covering, so the first and last letters go

parts.note: a safari is an expedition, especially in Africa

explanation.surface: An African expedition is laid bare abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exposed' strips SAFARI of its outer S and I.
explanation.definitionFit: Distant lands far away are overseas for some, so an example of being at a distance.

clue.text: Advertise footwear protecting back of legs

indicators.note: protecting says the footwear wraps around that letter

parts.note: a boot is footwear

indicators.note: back of says the final letter of the next word is taken

explanation.surface: Promote footwear that guards the backs of your legs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'protecting' puts S, the last of 'legs', inside BOOT.
explanation.definitionFit: To promote or plug a product is to push its sales, which advertising does.

clue.text: What covers individual's head?

indicators.note: in a down answer one piece covers another by sitting above it

parts.note: the top is the head of something
I, the Roman numeral one, means a single individual

explanation.surface: A riddle asking what goes on a person's head.
explanation.walkthrough: In the grid TOP sits over I. A topi is a pith helmet worn in hot countries.
explanation.definitionFit: A pith helmet, the sun hat of colonial India, is a piece of headgear.

clue.text: Uncertainty following start of dispute with union is spreading

indicators.note: following says the doubt word comes after the opening letter of the dispute
start of says only the opening letter of the next word is used

parts.note: an if is a doubt, as in 'no ifs or buts'
fusion is a joining together, a union

explanation.surface: Doubt about a quarrel with a trade union is spreading.
explanation.definitionFit: Diffusion is the dispersal of something through a space, the process of it spreading out.

clue.text: Seize two principal assets of greedy tech company

indicators.note: the two principal letters, the first pair of the next word, are taken

parts.note: Apple is the computer and phone company

explanation.surface: A greedy tech giant grabs a rival's top two assets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'two principal assets of' takes GR from 'greedy'.
explanation.definitionFit: To grapple with someone is to grip or grab hold of them, as in wrestling.

clue.text: Wife has to eat again outside tent?

indicators.note: outside says the dining word goes round the letter for wife

parts.note: to redine is to dine once more

explanation.surface: A wife has to eat another meal outside a camping tent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tent' is not canvas but a deep red Spanish wine, once used as communion wine; the question mark marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Tent is a dark Spanish wine from Alicante, an example of the red kind.
